rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a supplementary/lookup page, so §9's per-slide <=1-bold budget is waived by its reading-list/lookup-surface carve-out — but the handle cap (<=5 words, a SUB-SPAN, never a whole lead sentence) still binds and is violated on every bullet in both flagged chunks. Chunk 5 '## Design principles' (lines 115-126): all 7 bullets bold a complete lead clause ending in a period, then continue in plain prose, e.g. line 115 '**A skill never duplicates another's logic.** `/tdd` references `/testing`...' (bold span = 7 words, a full sentence, not a sub-span) and line 116 '**Orchestrators sequence and gate, never reimplement.**' (6 words, full sentence). Chunk 7 '## What's special about this stack' (lines 155-159): all 5 bullets do the same, e.g. line 158 '**Mandatory gates fire positionally.** `/ui` doesn't fire at session start...' — even where the bold span is <=5 words (line 155 '**Front-loaded read-only analysis.**' = 3 words, line 157 '**`/aios` is pure routing.**' = 4 words), it is still the ENTIRE lead sentence including terminal punctuation, which is the rule's own named violation shape verbatim: 'every bullet on a slide opens with a bolded sentence (the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture) — flatten to handles or prose.'
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Pull a short label out of each lead and unbold the rest (e.g. '**No duplication:** a skill never duplicates another's logic...') in both Design principles and What's special about this stack.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule 15's imperative/declarative mood split is defined for exercise vs. lecture files specifically ('Exercise `##` headings = imperative... Lecture headings = claims'). This file is a supplementary reference/progressive-reading page, not an exercise or lecture, so the binary mood contract doesn't bind it the same way; headings here are a mix of topical labels ('Diagrams', 'Skill catalog by phase') and one imperative worksheet heading ('Map your own kit'), consistent with a lookup/reference register rather than a violation of either mood. None of the diff's wording changes touched a `##` header itself.
